text:
morgan: FYI deploy to gpu-pool-ns failed in staging, 403 KMS decrypt error when controller tried to unwrap secrets. saw it during canary rollout.
anjali: ugh, seen that pattern before. paste of audit log:```{"kind":"Event","msg":"kms:Decrypt denied","sa":"deploy-controller-sa","key":"projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/prod/cryptoKeys/gpu-key"}```
kevin: can you kubectl auth can-i --as=system:serviceaccount:gpu-pool-ns:deploy-controller-sa decrypt --namespace=ignored? that'll tell us if SA has IAM bound identity.
morgan: ran it, got "no". but the rolebinding is weird — looks clusterrole binding to deploy-controller-sa in several namespaces. snippet:```kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: deploy-controller-global
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-controller-sa
  namespace: kube-system
roleRef:
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: deploy-controller```
anjali: yep, that's the culprit. we tightened least-priv rules last quarter and removed KMS decrypt from the cluster role but left an IAM grant expectation for namespace-scoped SA identities. so SA lost kms access in gpu-pool-ns.
kevin: two options: 1) grant a narrow IAM binding to the SA identity for the specific key (preferred), or 2) temporarily re-add the decrypt permission to the cluster role (fast but broad).
security-bot: Incident ticket created: SEC-2026-342 (auto). Notify oncall if escalates.
devops-oncall: what's the blast radius if we re-add decrypt to cluster role? any other controllers using it?
morgan: deploy-controller runs in 3 namespaces (gpu-pool-ns, inference-prod, staging). re-adding would restore staging but also give inference-prod access which we don't want.
anjali: propose: create a namespace-scoped RoleBinding in gpu-pool-ns that grants the minimal k8s verb to read secret CRs for only the deploy-controller-sa, plus create a short-lived IAM binding for the SA identity on the KMS key. Steps: 1) create k8s Role + RoleBinding, 2) request IAM key grant for subject "serviceAccount:gpu-pool-ns:deploy-controller-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" scoped to key and decrypt only, 3) patch deployment to use projected token (if not already).
kevin: patch example for Role:```apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  namespace: gpu-pool-ns
  name: deploy-controller-key-access
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["secrets"]
  verbs: ["get"]
---
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: deploy-controller-key-access
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-controller-sa
  namespace: gpu-pool-ns
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: deploy-controller-key-access
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io```
morgan: for IAM grant I can open a ticket to cloud-ops w/ principle and key, include TTL request (48h) for canary, then request permanent if PR reviewed.
anjali: also we should add an audit rule to detect KMS:Decrypt denies and alert before rollout. small CloudTrail/cloud audit sink: filter protoPayload.methodName="google.cloud.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND status.code!=0 -> alert.
kevin: can we add a test to CI that validates no controller uses cluster-wide decrypt permission? quick script: search terraform/iam for kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on cluster roles.
security-bot: checklist added to SEC-2026-342: [x] reproduce, [ ] narrow rolebinding PR, [ ] IAM request, [ ] CI test, [ ] postmortem note.
devops-oncall: timeline? staging rollback possible until fix?
morgan: canary paused, not rolling back yet. target to have RBAC patch + IAM short TTL within 6 hours. I'll open PR now: https://github.com/redwood/deployments/pull/4821 (draft).
kevin: reviewing the PR now. tiny nit: make Role name include tenant/gpu to be explicit.
anjali: once IAM grant applied, watch audit logs for 1 hour then flip to permanent binding if no anomalies. log query gives exact SA email so ops can verify.
morgan: noted. thanks all. tagging for DR and compliance: @security-bot please attach audit logs to ticket and mark for SOC review. :eyes: 
security-bot: attached last 500 events and flagged for SOC-ops review.
kevin: post-PR we should schedule a short follow-up to migrate any other namespaces that rely on cluster-level decrypt. maybe a batch migration doc.
morgan: agreed. will create a small runbook block under docs/runbooks/gpu-kms-access.md in the repo.
anjali: final reminder — do not reintroduce broad cluster decrypt perms. keep least-priv first.
morgan: closing loop after PR merges and IAM confirmed. will update SEC-2026-342 with timeline and remediation steps. :white_check_mark:
